questions.question: A sum of Rs. 12,500 is lent at 8% per annum simple interest for 3 years. What is the simple interest earned?
questions.trick: 8% for 3 years = 24% of principal. 24% of 12,500 = 3,000.

questions.question: Rs. 15,000 is invested at 10% per annum compound interest, compounded annually, for 2 years. What is the compound interest?
The difference between the compound interest and the simple interest on a certain sum for 2 years at 8% per annum is Rs. 96. What is the sum?
questions.trick: Difference (2 yrs) = P(R/100)^2; the difference equals the "interest on the first year's interest."

questions.question: A sum of money doubles itself in 8 years at simple interest. In how many years will the same sum become three times itself at the same rate?
questions.solution:
Doubling means interest earned = P. At SI, interest is constant each year, so P is earned in 8 years -> P/8 per year.
To triple, interest needed = 2P -> time = 2P / (P/8) = **16 years**.
questions.trick: (n-1) rule at SI. Double => interest = 1P in 8 yr. Triple => interest = 2P, so time = 2 x 8 = 16 yr.

questions.question: Rs. 8,000 is invested at 20% per annum compound interest, compounded half-yearly, for 1 year. What is the compound interest?
questions.solution: Half-yearly: rate = 10% per half-year, periods = 2. Amount = 8000 x (1.1)^2 = 8000 x 1.21 = 9,680. CI = **1,680**.
questions.trick: Half-yearly halves the rate (20% -> 10%) and doubles the periods (1 yr -> 2 half-years).

questions.question: A article costing Rs. 480 is sold at a profit of 15%. What is its selling price?
An article is sold for Rs. 736 at a loss of 8%. What was its cost price?
The marked price of an article is Rs. 1,200 and its cost price is Rs. 800. A discount of 20% is allowed on the marked price. What is the profit percentage?
Two successive discounts of 10% and 20% are given on an article. What is the single equivalent discount?
questions.solution: Net factor = (1 - 0.10)(1 - 0.20) = 0.9 x 0.8 = 0.72, i.e. 72% of MP is paid, so discount = **28%**.
questions.trick: Combined discount = a + b - (ab/100) = 10 + 20 - 2 = 28%.

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks his goods 40% above cost price and then allows a discount of 25% on the marked price. What is his profit or loss percentage?
questions.solution: Let CP = 100. MP = 140. SP = 140 x 0.75 = 105. Profit = 5, so profit% = **5%**.
questions.trick: Overall factor = 1.40 x 0.75 = 1.05 -> 5% profit.

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 12 days and B in 18 days. Working together, in how many days will they complete the work?
questions.solution: Take LCM(12, 18) = 36 units. A = 3 units/day, B = 2 units/day, together = 5 units/day. Time = 36/5 = **7.2 days**.

questions.question: A and B together can finish a work in 8 days. A alone can do it in 12 days. In how many days can B alone do the work?
questions.solution: B's one-day work = 1/8 - 1/12 = (3 - 2)/24 = 1/24, so B alone = **24 days**.
questions.trick: Product-over-difference: (8 x 12)/(12 - 8) = 96/4 = 24.

questions.question: 15 men can complete a piece of work in 20 days. How many days will 25 men take to complete the same work?
questions.solution: Men x Days is constant: 15 x 20 = 25 x D -> D = 300/25 = **12 days**.
questions.trick: More men, fewer days (inverse). 300 man-days / 25 men = 12.

questions.question: A is twice as efficient as B. Together they finish a work in 16 days. In how many days can A alone finish the work?
questions.solution: A : B efficiency = 2 : 1. Let B = 1, A = 2 units/day; together 3 units/day. Total work = 3 x 16 = 48 units. A alone = 48/2 = **24 days**.
questions.trick: If A is twice as efficient and together they take 16 days, A alone takes 16 x 3/2 = 24 days.

questions.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 6 hours and pipe B can empty it in 9 hours. If both pipes are opened together, in how long will the tank be filled?
questions.solution: Net fill rate = 1/6 - 1/9 = (3 - 2)/18 = 1/18 per hour, so time = **18 hours**.
questions.trick: Fill minus empty; net one-part per 18 hours means 18 hours to fill.

questions.question: A car travels at a uniform speed of 60 km/h. How long will it take to cover a distance of 210 km?
questions.solution: Time = Distance / Speed = 210 / 60 = **3.5 hours**.

questions.question: A train 180 metres long is running at 72 km/h. How much time will it take to cross a pole?
questions.solution: 72 km/h = 72 x 5/18 = 20 m/s. To cross a pole, distance = train length = 180 m. Time = 180/20 = **9 seconds**.
questions.trick: To cross a pole, only the train's own length matters.

questions.question: A train 240 metres long, moving at 20 m/s, crosses a platform 360 metres long. How much time does it take?
questions.solution: Total distance = 240 + 360 = 600 m. Time = 600/20 = **30 seconds**.
questions.trick: To cross a platform, distance = train length + platform length.

questions.question: Two trains, 120 m and 130 m long, are running in opposite directions at 54 km/h and 36 km/h respectively. How much time will they take to cross each other?
questions.solution: Opposite directions -> add speeds: 54 + 36 = 90 km/h = 25 m/s. Total length = 120 + 130 = 250 m. Time = 250/25 = **10 seconds**.
questions.trick: Crossing each other -> relative speed x sum of lengths.

questions.question: A boat covers 28 km downstream in 2 hours and 16 km upstream in 2 hours. What is the speed of the stream?
questions.solution: Downstream speed = 28/2 = 14 km/h. Upstream speed = 16/2 = 8 km/h. Stream = (14 - 8)/2 = **3 km/h**.
questions.trick: Stream speed = (downstream - upstream)/2; boat speed = (downstream + upstream)/2.

questions.question: The average of 5 numbers is 27. If one of the numbers, which is 15, is removed, what is the average of the remaining numbers?
questions.solution: Sum of 5 numbers = 5 x 27 = 135. Remove 15 -> 120 over 4 numbers -> 120/4 = **30**.

questions.question: The average age of 30 students in a class is 14 years. When the teacher's age is included, the average increases by 1 year. What is the teacher's age?
questions.solution: Total of 31 people = 31 x 15 = 465. Total of 30 students = 30 x 14 = 420. Teacher = 465 - 420 = **45**.
questions.trick: New member's value = new average + (old count x increase) = 15 + 30 x 1 = 45.

questions.question: What is the average of the first five multiples of 6?
questions.trick: For an evenly spaced set, average = middle term = 18.

questions.question: The average weight of A, B and C is 60 kg. The average weight of A and B is 55 kg, and that of B and C is 65 kg. What is the weight of B?
The average of 20 numbers was calculated as 35. Later it was found that one number was read as 18 instead of the correct 78. What is the correct average?
questions.solution: Wrong sum = 20 x 35 = 700. Correction = 78 - 18 = +60. Correct sum = 760. Correct average = 760/20 = **38**.
questions.trick: Change in average = correction/count = 60/20 = 3; 35 + 3 = 38.

questions.question: The present ages of A and B are in the ratio 5 : 7. After 6 years the ratio of their ages will be 3 : 4. What is the present age of A?
The sum of the ages of a father and his son is 60 years. Six years ago the father's age was five times the son's age. What is the son's present age?
questions.solution: Let son = s, father = 60 - s. Six years ago: (60 - s - 6) = 5(s - 6) -> 54 - s = 5s - 30 -> 6s = 84 -> s = **14**. (Check: father 46; 6 yrs ago 40 = 5 x 8.)

questions.question: A is older than B by 6 years. Ten years ago, A's age was three times B's age. What is A's present age?
questions.solution: Let B ten years ago = b, then A = 3b. Now A = 3b + 10, B = b + 10; difference 2b = 6 -> b = 3. A now = 3(3) + 10 = **19**. (Check: B now 13, difference 6; 10 yrs ago 9 = 3 x 3.)

questions.question: The present ages of P and Q are in the ratio 3 : 5. Q is 8 years older than P. What will be P's age after 5 years?
questions.solution: Ratio 3 : 5; difference 2 parts = 8 -> 1 part = 4. P = 3 x 4 = 12. After 5 years = **17**.

questions.question: A man's present age is three times his son's age. Fifteen years ago, the man's age was nine times the son's age. What is the man's present age?
questions.solution: Let son = s, man = 3s. Fifteen years ago: 3s - 15 = 9(s - 15) -> 3s - 15 = 9s - 135 -> 6s = 120 -> s = 20. Man = 3 x 20 = **60**. (Check: 15 yrs ago 45 = 9 x 5.)

questions.question: Rs. 720 is divided between two persons in the ratio 3 : 5. What is the larger share?
questions.solution: Total parts = 3 + 5 = 8; one part = 720/8 = 90. Larger share = 5 x 90 = **450**.

questions.question: Two numbers are in the ratio 5 : 8. If each is increased by 6, the ratio becomes 7 : 10. What are the two numbers?
If A : B = 2 : 3 and B : C = 4 : 5, then A : B : C is:
questions.trick: Scale each ratio so the common term (B) matches.

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 100 is divided among three friends in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5. What is the largest share?
questions.solution: Total parts = 2 + 3 + 5 = 10; one part = 100/10 = 10. Largest = 5 x 10 = **50**.

questions.question: If 40% of A equals 60% of B, then A : B is:
What is 35% of 640?
A number when increased by 25% becomes 350. What is the original number?
questions.trick: Increase by 25% = x 5/4, so original = 350 x 4/5 = 280.

questions.question: If the price of a commodity increases by 20%, by what percentage must a family reduce its consumption so that the expenditure remains unchanged?
questions.solution: Required reduction = increase/(100 + increase) = 20/120 = 1/6 = **16 2/3%**.
questions.trick: Price up r% -> consumption down [r/(100 + r)] x 100 %.

questions.question: In an examination, 40% marks are required to pass. A candidate scored 180 marks and failed by 20 marks. What are the maximum marks?
The population of a town is 20,000. It increases by 10% in the first year and decreases by 10% in the second year. What is the population at the end of two years?
questions.trick: +10% then -10% always gives a net -1% (= -x^2/100 for x = 10).

questions.question: 40 litres of a mixture contain milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1. How much water must be added so that the ratio becomes 3 : 2?
questions.solution: Milk = 3/4 x 40 = 30 L, water = 10 L. Let w litres of water be added: 30/(10 + w) = 3/2 -> 60 = 30 + 3w -> w = **10 litres**. (Milk stays constant.)

questions.question: In what ratio must rice costing Rs. 40 per kg be mixed with rice costing Rs. 60 per kg so that the mixture costs Rs. 48 per kg?
questions.solution: By alligation: cheaper : dearer = (60 - 48) : (48 - 40) = 12 : 8 = **3 : 2**.

questions.question: A 40-litre solution contains 10% water and the rest alcohol. How much water must be added to make the water content 25% of the new solution?
questions.solution: Water = 10% of 40 = 4 L; alcohol = 36 L (unchanged). For water to be 25%, alcohol is 75% of new total -> new total = 36/0.75 = 48 L. Water added = 48 - 40 = **8 litres**.

questions.question: From a vessel containing 50 litres of pure milk, 5 litres are drawn out and replaced with water. This process is repeated once more. How much pure milk remains in the vessel?
questions.trick: Replacement formula: initial x (1 - drawn/total)^n.

questions.question: A vessel contains 25 litres of a mixture of milk and water in the ratio 3 : 2. If 5 litres of the mixture is removed and replaced with 5 litres of water, what is the new ratio of milk to water?
questions.solution: Initial: milk 15 L, water 10 L. Removing 5 L of a 3 : 2 mix removes 3 L milk and 2 L water -> milk 12, water 8. Add 5 L water -> water 13. Ratio = **12 : 13**.

questions.question: A invests Rs. 5,000 and B invests Rs. 7,000 in a business for one year. If the total annual profit is Rs. 3,600, what is B's share?
questions.solution: Ratio of investments = 5000 : 7000 = 5 : 7. B's share = 7/12 x 3600 = **2,100**.

questions.question: A invests Rs. 8,000 for 12 months and B invests Rs. 12,000 for 6 months. If the total profit is Rs. 2,800, what is A's share?
questions.trick: Share is proportional to (amount x time).

questions.question: A and B invest amounts in the ratio 4 : 5. A keeps his money invested for 12 months and B for 9 months. If the total profit is Rs. 3,100, what is B's share?
Three partners A, B and C invest Rs. 6,000, Rs. 8,000 and Rs. 10,000 respectively in a business. If the total profit is Rs. 7,200, what is C's share?
A starts a business with Rs. 12,000. After 4 months, B joins with Rs. 18,000. At the end of the year, the total profit is Rs. 5,100. What is each partner's share?
questions.trick: Larger capital for fewer months can equal smaller capital for more months — always compare (amount x time).
